title: Design System: Harry Dresden — Wizard for Hire

display.purpose: Page hero H1 only, one per page, bottom-anchored in the hero.

body.purpose: All paragraph copy, in-universe voice, max ~65ch.

label.purpose: Nav items, eyebrows, footer categories, case ref numbers, redaction tags — never paragraph copy.

micro-label.purpose: One size down from Case Label (0.65rem) for secondary chrome metadata: folder status lines, pinned-card status lines.

board-body.purpose: 0.95rem tightened body step used only in the detective board's fixed-width case-summary card.

shadows.name: physical-card
shadows.purpose: Pinned board notes and polaroids — simulates a real object resting on/pinned to a surface.

shadows.name: folder-stack
shadows.purpose: Manila folder body and photo stack on the Case Files desk.

shadows.name: pin-drop
shadows.purpose: The small red pin marker on every board card and polaroid.

shadows.name: ground-scrim
shadows.purpose: Two-stop gradient over every hero photo, keyed to that world's own ground color rather than neutral black, for text legibility.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: Default motion for anything settling into place — folder rest state, board card flight. Deliberately not an overshoot/bounce curve.

motion.name: ease-shoo
motion.purpose: Other case folders scattering off-screen when one is opened.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Amber-filled call to action, used across every world (e.g. "See services", "Open a case").
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-block; background: #c9a876; color: #0d0c0f; font-family: 'Special Elite', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 12px 24px; border-radius: 2px; transition: background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #efe6d4; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Outline button used for secondary actions; hover shifts to the current page world's accent color rather than amber.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-block; background: transparent; color: #efe6d4; font-family: 'Special Elite', 'Courier New', monospace; font-size: 0.8rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; text-transform: uppercase; padding: 12px 24px; border-radius: 2px; border: 1px solid rgba(239,230,212,0.3); transition: border-color 0.2s ease, color 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { border-color: #d94fd0; color: #d94fd0; }

components.name: Case Label
components.description: The recurring typewriter eyebrow/tag used for nav items, section eyebrows, footer categories, and redaction tags.
components.css: .ds-case-label { font-family: 'Special Elite', 'Courier New', monospace; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; font-size: 0.72rem; color: #c9a876; }

components.name: Pinned Note Card
components.description: Detective-board card: paper-colored, sharp corners, a red circular pin at the top edge, deep drop shadow to read as a physical object.
components.html:
Case Summary

A simple infidelity case gets complicated fast…
components.css: .ds-pinned-note { position: relative; background: #f2ead6; padding: 16px; box-shadow: 0 25px 50px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.5); color: #1c130a; } .ds-pin { position: absolute; top: -8px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #b3231c; box-shadow: 0 2px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.5); }

components.name: Manila Case Folder
components.description: Signature component: fanned paper sheets, a manila folder body with tab, and a paperclipped polaroid pinned to the front cover. Rest state carries a small deterministic rotation; hover fans the papers and lifts the photo.
components.html: No. 01 · Storm Front
components.css: .ds-case-folder { position: relative; width: 220px; aspect-ratio: 4/3; transform: rotate(-3deg); } .ds-folder-body { position: absolute; inset: 22% 0 0 0; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #d9bd85 0%, #c2a36a 100%); box-shadow: 0 20px 25px -5px rgba(0,0,0,0.35); } .ds-folder-tab { position: absolute; top: -16px; left: 16px; width: 96px; height: 16px; background: #d9bd85; } .ds-folder-label { position: absolute; bottom: 12px; left: 12px; right: 12px; font-family: 'Big Shoulders Display', sans-serif; font-weight: 700; color: #0d0c0f; } .ds-folder-photo { position: absolute; top: -28px; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%) rotate(4deg); width: 80px; height: 96px; background: #fff; box-shadow: 0 25px 50px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.5); }

narrative.overview: This site is staged as Harry Dresden's actual business site — the modern web presence for the wizard-detective from Jim Butcher's Dresden Files, run in-universe. The governing idea is that Harry's whole world lives across four distinct visual "cases," one per section, each its own atmosphere, held together by a single recurring artifact: the paper case file. Nav, footer, buttons, and labels are dressed as dossier chrome — typewriter labels, amber rule lines, parchment tones — so a visitor always knows which drawer of Harry's practice they've opened even as the backdrop shifts from neon-lit street to black-and-white detective office to candlelit study to gothic threshold to a literal green-felt case-file desk.
keyCharacteristics: Four fully-committed worlds (Neon Threshold, Classic Hardboiled, The Grimoire, Gothic Threshold) plus a fifth interactive world (The Case Board) — not four color reskins of one layout, but four distinct atmospheres
Dossier chrome (nav, footer, buttons, labels) stays visually constant across every world as the connective thread
Typewriter/case-file motifs (redaction bars, case numbers, "Ref." tags, pinned photographs) recur as the system's signature device
Photography-led hero sections: every page opens on a full-bleed generated photographic scene, never a flat color hero

rules.name: The One Thread Rule
rules.body: Dossier amber (#c9a876 / #e8b563) is the only color permitted to cross world boundaries. A new world may introduce its own palette freely, but nav, footer, buttons, and case-labels stay amber-on-dossier-ink regardless of which world's page they sit on.

rules.name: The Drenched World Rule
rules.body: A page world is not "dossier chrome plus one accent swapped in" — it's a full palette commitment (ground, accent, accent-2/mist) applied at page scale via a full-bleed photographic hero, gradient-faded into the page background of the same ground color.

rules.name: The Typewriter-Never-Reads Rule
rules.body: Special Elite (the case/label face) is reserved for short administrative strings only — labels, numbers, nav — never body paragraphs. It authenticates the dossier conceit without hurting readability.

rules.name: The Physical Object Rule
rules.body: Shadows exist only under things that are meant to read as physical objects sitting on or pinned to a surface (case folders, polaroids, pinned note cards) — never as generic card/panel elevation for UI grouping.

dos: Do keep dossier amber (#c9a876 / #e8b563) as the only color permitted on shared chrome (nav, footer, primary buttons, case labels) regardless of which world's page it sits on.
Do open every page on a full-bleed photographic hero with a bottom-anchored headline, gradient-faded to the page's own ground color.
Do commit each page world fully (ground + accent + accent-2/mist) rather than blending worlds or introducing a shared "brand" hue beyond amber.
Do reserve Special Elite (typewriter face) for short administrative/label strings only.
Do keep corners sharp (rounded-sm at most) everywhere — this is a paper-and-dossier system, not a soft app-UI system.
donts: Don't introduce a fifth shared accent color beyond dossier amber; per-world accents stay scoped to their own page.
Don't round any component beyond rounded-sm (2px) — no rounded-lg/rounded-xl/pill shapes anywhere in this system.
Don't use Special Elite for paragraph body copy; it's a label face only.
Don't add generic UI drop-shadows to non-physical elements (nav bars, plain content sections); shadows are reserved for things simulating physical paper objects.

Don't flatten the Case Files page's world-specific interaction (fanned papers, shared-element flight, red string) into a generic modal — it is this system's signature component and should stay distinctive.
